text: Every chapter in this course is a working part of the same Sentinel deployment, and this capstone is where they stop being seven separate topics and start being the thing Lessons 29 through 31 just ran for real — a custom detection, a full investigation, and a multi-stage incident closed start to finish. No single chapter was ever meant to do that job alone.

Chapter 1 is the Log Analytics workspace and connectors every log in this course landed on. Chapter 2 is KQL itself — the self-join that caught impossible travel, and the hunting queries that checked for broader compromise. Chapters 3 and 4 turned that query into a rule that runs on its own, and into workbooks that watch the same data continuously.

Chapter 5 is Defender XDR — the actual source of Lesson 31's phishing alert, unifying endpoint, email, and identity signals into one unified portal. Chapter 6 is the investigation graph, entity timeline, and hunting query that Lessons 30 and 31 both ran to confirm what happened and how far it reached. Chapter 7 is the playbook that disabled a compromised account in seconds, before an analyst even opened the case.

Lesson 31's case is the clearest proof this has to work as one system. A rule with no entity mapping never correlates with the phishing alert. A correlated incident with no automation rule and playbook behind it waits minutes for a human to act. A disabled account with no investigation graph, timeline, and hunting query behind it never gets confirmed as contained instead of still spreading. Every chapter is load-bearing for the ones that come after it.

That's the full course — from what Sentinel actually is, to writing a custom KQL detection, investigating the incident it created, and watching it correlate with Defender XDR, respond through a playbook, and close with a clear, defensible resolution. Course complete. Next up in this path: Incident Response, Threat Hunting & SOC Capstone, which closes the Job-Ready Foundation stage.
